instrumentation: K-indie basslines, warehouse techno, street busker guitar
character_short: a packed university nightlife district with buskers and pop-up galleries at midnight
narrative: The nightlife heart of Seoul's university district, centered on Hongik University and known since the 1990s for its indie-music clubs, street busking, and underground art scene. Streets fill with pop-up galleries and live performers from evening into the small hours, giving it a dense, youth-driven energy distinct from the rest of the city.

instrumentation: ceremonial court music, stone courtyard reverb, temple bell
character_short: a 14th-century royal palace at dawn, guards changing in ceremonial silence
narrative: The principal royal palace of the Joseon Dynasty, construction began in 1395 under King Taejo shortly after Seoul became the capital. The daily changing-of-the-guard ceremony and the palace's stone courtyards give it a formal, ceremonial stillness in the middle of a dense modern city.

instrumentation: glossy K-pop synth-pop, sidechain-pumped bass, glass-tower shimmer
character_short: a glittering high-rise district of designer boutiques and rooftop bars
narrative: Seoul's glass-tower business and luxury-retail district, globally known since the 2012 song of the same name, built around wide boulevards, designer flagship stores, and Coex Mall. It reads as polished, fast-paced, and unmistakably wealthy compared to the historic core just north of the river.

instrumentation: solo daegeum flute, dawn stillness, wooden windchime
character_short: a 600-year-old hillside village of traditional wooden houses at sunrise
narrative: A hillside neighborhood of traditional hanok houses between Gyeongbokgung and Changdeokgung palaces, continuously inhabited for roughly six centuries. Narrow alleys and tiled rooflines make it one of Seoul's few places where the pre-modern city is still legible at street level.

instrumentation: twinkling glockenspiel, distant city hum, cable-car cable creak
character_short: a mountaintop tower over the whole skyline at night, love-locks glinting on the railing
narrative: A 236-meter communications and observation tower atop Namsan mountain, completed in 1969 and opened to the public in 1980, now one of Seoul's most recognizable landmarks. Thousands of padlocks left by couples on its terrace fences have made it a well-known symbolic site for relationships in the city.

instrumentation: sleek electronic pulse, LED-panel shimmer, fashion-week footsteps
character_short: a curving titanium spaceship of a building hosting fashion shows and light-art festivals
narrative: A neo-futurist exhibition and design complex designed by Zaha Hadid, opened in 2014 on the site of a former stadium and historic market area. Its curved, seamless steel-and-concrete form stands in deliberate contrast to the surrounding wholesale-fashion district it sits within.

instrumentation: summer house music, seagulls, boardwalk crowd hum
character_short: Korea's most famous beach backed by glittering resort towers in high summer
narrative: Korea's most famous urban beach, backed by a dense skyline of high-rise resort towers, drawing enormous summer crowds along roughly 1.5km of sand. It is the clearest single symbol of Busan's identity as a beach city that is also a major metropolis.

instrumentation: lo-fi hip-hop, wind chimes, hillside echo
character_short: a pastel hillside village stacked like a Korean Cinque Terre, murals on every wall
narrative: A hillside neighborhood of pastel-colored houses built by war refugees in the 1950s, later revitalized as a public art project starting in 2009 and now often compared to a Korean Santorini or Cinque Terre. Murals, sculptures, and small galleries are woven directly into the still-residential streets.

instrumentation: vendor calls, gull cries, harbor engine drone, brass
character_short: Korea's largest seafood market, boats unloading at dawn, vendors shouting prices
narrative: Korea's largest seafood market, active on the Busan waterfront since the aftermath of the Korean War, where vendors sell live catch straight off fishing boats each morning. The building itself, rebuilt several times, remains a working market rather than a tourist reconstruction.

instrumentation: crashing waves, seabird cry, lighthouse foghorn
character_short: sheer cliffs dropping into the sea, a lighthouse at the end of a pine-forest trail
narrative: A cliffside park at Busan's southern tip where a lighthouse trail runs along dramatic sea cliffs dropping straight into the water, with a small train looping visitors through pine forest. It is one of the calmest, least urban corners of an otherwise dense port city.

instrumentation: sizzling street-food grill, film-reel clatter, neon marquee hum
character_short: Busan's original film-festival district, street-food stalls sizzling under movie-star handprints
narrative: The Nampo-dong plaza that gave the Busan International Film Festival its name before the festival's main venues moved elsewhere; today it's a dense street-food and cinema district with handprints of past festival guests set into the pavement. It carries the city's film-industry identity at street level, independent of the festival's official venues.

instrumentation: sizzling street-food percussion, festival drum, crowd chatter
character_short: a 500-year-old night market of sizzling street food and lantern-lit stalls
narrative: One of Korea's three great traditional markets, trading on this site in some form for roughly 500 years, today known for its night-market food stalls and dense maze of textile and general-goods shops. It reflects Daegu's historic identity as a market and textile city more directly than almost any other single site.

instrumentation: acoustic guitar, cicada drone, mountain wind
character_short: a forested mountain park overlooking the city, cable cars gliding through pines
narrative: A forested mountain park on Daegu's southern edge, reached by cable car, offering panoramic views over the entire city basin. It functions as the city's main escape into quiet, forested terrain without leaving the metropolitan area.

instrumentation: temple bell, monk chant, pine-forest hush
character_short: a mountain temple guarded by a towering stone Buddha, incense drifting through pine trees
narrative: A major Buddhist temple on Palgongsan mountain founded in the Silla period, home to a towering modern stone Buddha statue completed in the 1990s. Incense and pine forest give the approach a slow, meditative pace distinct from the city below.

instrumentation: carnival ride chime, pop-fireworks crackle, Ferris-wheel motor hum
character_short: an amusement park lighting up at dusk beneath a spinning observation tower
narrative: An amusement park and adjoining public park in central Daegu, home to the 202-meter Duryu Tower and, seasonally, a large cherry-blossom and light-festival display. It is Daegu's main concentrated site for organized entertainment and nightlife lighting.

instrumentation: Chinese brass ensemble, sizzling wok percussion, harbor bell
character_short: Korea's oldest Chinatown, red lanterns and the smell of jjajangmyeon at dusk
narrative: Korea's only official Chinatown, established in 1884 the year after Incheon's port opened to international trade, once home to over 10,000 Chinese residents. It is the acknowledged birthplace of jjajangmyeon, the black-bean noodle dish now eaten nationwide.

instrumentation: glassy ambient synth, canal water lapping, distant traffic hum
character_short: a brand-new planned city of glass towers and seawater canals
narrative: The central green space of Songdo International Business District, a smart city built from reclaimed land starting in 2003, with a seawater canal running through landscaped grounds beside glass office towers. It represents a deliberately engineered, 21st-century counterpoint to Incheon's 19th-century port district.

instrumentation: carnival calliope, seagulls, tide bell
character_short: an old-fashioned seaside amusement pier with a ferris wheel at sunset
narrative: A small seaside peninsula and old amusement district facing Incheon's inner harbor, long popular for its ferris wheel, seafood restaurants, and sunset views over the water. It carries an older, slightly faded carnival character compared to the newer developments elsewhere in the city.

instrumentation: stone-on-stone resonance, open-field wind, distant crow call
character_short: 5,000-year-old stone tombs standing alone in open farmland, older than the pyramids
narrative: A UNESCO World Heritage cluster of prehistoric dolmens on Ganghwa Island, among the largest concentrations of megalithic tombs in the world, dating back roughly 2,000-3,000 years. The site sits in quiet farmland, a sharp contrast to Incheon's industrial and commercial core nearby.

instrumentation: brass memorial fanfare, harbor foghorn, park-bench quiet
character_short: a hilltop war-memorial park overlooking the harbor where the Incheon Landing began
narrative: Korea's first Western-style public park, opened in 1888 on a hill overlooking Incheon's harbor, home to a statue of General Douglas MacArthur commemorating the 1950 Incheon Landing. Its hilltop position gives sweeping views over the port that shaped the city's modern history.

instrumentation: solo daegeum, pine wind, distant temple bell
character_short: a granite-peaked mountain sacred to the city, pine forest and quiet trails
narrative: A granite-peaked mountain overlooking Gwangju, considered sacred to the city and designated a national park in 2013, laced with pine forest and quiet hiking trails. It offers the clearest contrast in the region between Gwangju's dense urban core and untouched nature just beyond it.

instrumentation: muted trumpet, rain on tile roofs, sparse piano
character_short: a century-old hillside quarter of missionary houses turned into galleries
narrative: A hillside neighborhood built up by Western missionaries from the early 1900s, its early-20th-century houses and mission buildings now repurposed as galleries and cafes. The area preserves a distinct layer of Gwangju's history not found in its more purely Korean historic districts.

instrumentation: robotic-arm servo whine, conveyor-belt clank, assembly-line rhythm
character_short: a car rolling off the line every few seconds inside a vast automated assembly plant
narrative: Kia's major manufacturing complex in Gwangju, one of the region's largest employers, producing SUVs and other models for both domestic and export markets on a large integrated assembly campus. It anchors Gwangju's identity as an industrial as well as a cultural and historical city.

instrumentation: solo funeral bell, wind through pines, quiet marble hush
character_short: the memorial cemetery for Korea's 1980 pro-democracy uprising, solemn rows of white headstones
narrative: The official memorial cemetery for civilians killed during the May 1980 Gwangju Uprising, when a pro-democracy protest was suppressed by military force. Rows of white headstones and a solemn memorial hall make it Korea's central site for remembering the event that helped shape the country's democratic transition.

instrumentation: steam hiss, soft vibraphone, warm pad drone
character_short: a centuries-old hot spring resort town wrapped in mineral steam
narrative: A hot-spring resort district in Daejeon with a documented history stretching back centuries, long used as a place of rest and recovery. Steam rising from mineral baths gives the neighborhood a slower, warmer character than the research-driven districts elsewhere in the city.

instrumentation: birdsong, koto-like pluck, leaf rustle
character_short: a quiet botanical garden in the middle of the science city
narrative: A large botanical garden in central Daejeon, one of the biggest urban arboretums in Korea, with themed gardens and greenhouses spread across a quiet, tree-lined campus. It functions as a deliberate green counterweight to the science-and-technology identity that otherwise defines the city.

instrumentation: server-room hum, cleanroom whir, quiet lab keyboard clatter
character_short: Korea's largest research cluster, satellite labs and robotics institutes humming quietly behind glass
narrative: Korea's designated national science-research cluster, established from Daedeok Science Town (approved 1973), now home to KAIST and over half the country's public research institutes. It is the concrete, campus-like embodiment of Daejeon's self-image as Korea's science capital.

instrumentation: retro-futuristic synth chime, fountain splash, science-museum ambience
character_short: the leftover grounds of Korea's 1993 World Expo, a golden tower rising over fountains
narrative: The former site of Expo '93, Daejeon's 1993 World's Fair themed around "The Challenge of a New Road to Development," anchored by the futuristic Hanbit Tower. The park preserves a snapshot of 1990s techno-optimism that still defines part of the city's public identity.

instrumentation: bamboo wind chime, river flow, soft flute
character_short: the world's largest riverside bamboo forest, cutting through an industrial city
narrative: A riverside park through central Ulsan built around what is described as the world's largest riverside bamboo forest, offering a green corridor through an otherwise heavily industrial city. Bamboo groves and river paths give it a markedly calmer character than the shipyards a short distance away.

instrumentation: ocean swell, lighthouse foghorn drone, gull cry
character_short: mainland Korea's easternmost point, first sunrise of the year over open ocean
narrative: Mainland Korea's easternmost point, marked by a lighthouse and famous as one of the first places in the country to see the New Year's sunrise. Open ocean views and a coastal park make it a naturally quiet counterpoint to Ulsan's industrial economy.

instrumentation: stamping-press thud, welding-robot spark crackle, dockside crane hum
character_short: the world's largest single automobile plant, five factories producing a car every few seconds
narrative: The world's largest single automobile assembly plant complex, established in 1968, spanning roughly 5,000,000 square meters across five integrated factories with an annual capacity of over a million vehicles. It is the single largest concrete expression of Ulsan's identity as Korea's industrial capital.

instrumentation: Goliath-crane groan, steel-plate welding hiss, dry-dock horn blast
character_short: a shipyard building some of the largest vessels on Earth, cranes the size of skyscrapers
narrative: The world's largest shipyard, built along roughly 4km of Ulsan's coastline, capable of constructing some of the largest vessels ever built by a single yard. Cranes, dry docks, and constant welding and fabrication activity define the sound and scale of this stretch of coast.

instrumentation: minimalist synth pad, water ripple, distant construction hum
character_short: a brand-new artificial lake park at the heart of Korea's planned administrative capital
narrative: An artificial lake park at the center of Sejong, South Korea's newest planned administrative capital, built as green infrastructure alongside the government complex rather than added after the fact. Its deliberate, still-young landscaping reflects a city built garden-first.

instrumentation: acoustic fingerstyle guitar, river current, evening cricket
character_short: a quiet riverside promenade at dusk in Korea's newest city
narrative: A riverside promenade along the Geum River running through Sejong, offering a quiet walking and cycling corridor in a city still filling in around it. The relative emptiness compared to older Korean cities is itself characteristic of Sejong's newness.

instrumentation: quiet corridor echo, rooftop-garden breeze, official footsteps
character_short: a decentralized government complex with the world's longest rooftop garden connecting 15 ministries
narrative: The seat of roughly three dozen Korean government ministries, relocated from Seoul starting in 2012, topped by a Guinness World Record-holding 3.6km rooftop garden spanning multiple buildings. It is the literal administrative reason Sejong exists as a city at all.

instrumentation: martial drum, brass fanfare, stone-wall echo
character_short: an 18th-century UNESCO fortress wall you can walk the full 5.7km circuit of
narrative: An 18th-century UNESCO World Heritage fortress wall encircling Suwon's old town for roughly 5.7km, built during the reign of King Jeongjo and still fully walkable today. It makes Suwon the only remaining completely walled city in South Korea.

instrumentation: acoustic guitar, birdsong, tree-lined breeze
character_short: a crescent-shaped river island famous for its tree-lined autumn paths
narrative: A crescent-shaped river island known for its long, symmetrical tree-lined paths, especially famous for autumn foliage and as a filming location for a well-known Korean drama. Its car-free, park-like layout gives it a deliberately romantic, unhurried atmosphere.

instrumentation: minimalist piano, paper rustle, concrete reverb
character_short: a planned town built entirely around publishing houses and bookshops
narrative: A planned publishing town north of Seoul purpose-built around Korea's book industry, housing publishing houses, printing facilities, and bookshop-cafes in architecturally distinct buildings. It is one of the few urban areas in Korea organized entirely around a single cultural industry.

instrumentation: cleanroom hum, glass-elevator chime, semiconductor-fab whir
character_short: Samsung Electronics' 390-acre headquarters campus, 35,000 engineers working behind glass towers
narrative: Samsung Electronics' primary headquarters and R&D campus in Suwon, spanning roughly 390 acres with tens of thousands of employees across dozens of office and lab buildings. Since the company's 1969 founding in Suwon, it has grown into one of the most consequential technology addresses in the world.

instrumentation: farmer's percussion band, tightrope-walker gasp, thatched-roof wind
character_short: a recreated Joseon-dynasty village with 260 relocated houses and live folk performances
narrative: A large open-air museum in Yongin recreating a late-Joseon-era village with over 260 relocated and reconstructed traditional houses, organized by region and social class. Unlike a genuine historic village, it is built specifically for visitors, with daily performances and craft demonstrations rather than resident life.

instrumentation: solo cello, alpine wind, sparse piano
character_short: Korea's most dramatic granite peaks, glowing at sunrise above cloud forest
narrative: Home to some of Korea's most dramatic granite peaks and considered the country's finest for autumn foliage, with trails ranging from short walks to serious alpine hikes. Cloud forest and exposed rock faces give it a rugged, elemental character distinct from Korea's gentler inland mountains.

instrumentation: lo-fi coffee-shop beat, ocean ambience, indie guitar
character_short: Korea's coffee capital, cafes lining a pine-backed beach
narrative: A coastal city on Gangwon's east coast known nationally as Korea's coffee capital, with cafes lined along a pine-backed beach, alongside the UNESCO-recognized Gangneung Danoje Festival held each June. It blends a slow, cafe-culture pace with deep traditional-ritual roots.

instrumentation: acoustic mandolin, lake ripple, chalkboard-cafe hum
character_short: a lake-ringed city famous for grilled chicken and slow afternoons on the water
narrative: A lake-ringed city famous for dak-galbi (spicy grilled chicken) and for slow afternoons spent on the water, with Uiam Lake and Soyang Lake bordering much of the urban area. Its identity leans toward relaxed, food-and-water leisure rather than fast urban energy.

instrumentation: fir-forest hush, temple wind chime, stone pagoda stillness
character_short: a nine-story stone pagoda in a fir forest at the foot of Odaesan's highest peaks
narrative: A nine-story stone pagoda and temple complex set in a fir forest at the base of Odaesan's high peaks, among Korea's most architecturally significant surviving Buddhist sites. The dense fir forest surrounding it creates an unusually hushed approach even by temple standards.

instrumentation: monorail motor whir, wind over open plain, distant binocular click
character_short: an observatory looking straight into the DMZ and a North Korean propaganda village beyond
narrative: An observation post near the DMZ in Gangwon's north, offering views into the demilitarized zone and, on clear days, into North Korean territory. Its subject matter gives it a solemn, historically weighted character unlike anywhere else on this list.
photo_artist: U.S. Army EIGHTHARMY by Pfc. Yun Hyuk Kim

instrumentation: folk guitar, light percussion, flowing water
character_short: a river valley threading between limestone peaks, kayaked at golden hour
narrative: A river-valley town where the Namhan River threads between limestone peaks, popular for kayaking and scenic cruises at golden hour. Its geology, similar in spirit to Chinese scroll-painting landscapes, makes it one of the more visually distinctive inland towns in Korea.

instrumentation: wooden moktak percussion, chanting, forest silence
character_short: a mountain temple valley so quiet you can hear pine needles fall
narrative: A mountain temple valley home to Beopjusa, one of Korea's most important Buddhist temples, set among peaks quiet enough that falling pine needles are audible. It anchors Chungcheongbuk-do's reputation for temple stillness alongside its river valleys.

instrumentation: cleanroom air-filter hum, silicon-wafer chime, fab-line drone
character_short: a sprawling memory-chip fabrication campus, cleanrooms manufacturing the world's DRAM
narrative: A major semiconductor manufacturing complex in Cheongju producing memory chips including HBM for AI applications, backed by a 15.5 trillion won expansion of the surrounding Cheongju Technopolis. It represents Chungcheongbuk-do's rapid pivot from a purely agricultural economy toward advanced manufacturing.

instrumentation: boat-engine putter, lake ripple, valley echo
character_short: a vast reservoir threading through steep valleys, cruise boats crossing calm water
narrative: A large reservoir threading through steep valleys in northern Chungcheongbuk-do, used for cruise boats and water recreation across calm, wide water. Its scale and the surrounding hills give it a more expansive, open feel than the province's narrower river valleys.
photo_artist: Jared Broad from Auckland, New Zealand

instrumentation: gayageum, temple bell, river mist ambience
character_short: the last capital of the Baekje kingdom, ruins wrapped in river mist
narrative: The last capital of the Baekje Kingdom (as Sabi, 538-660 CE), its ruins wrapped in river mist along the Geum River and now part of the UNESCO-listed Baekje Historic Areas. It preserves the memory of a kingdom whose art and architecture influenced early Japan.

instrumentation: tide wash, seagulls, mellow acoustic guitar
character_short: a wide tidal-flat beach on the west coast at low tide
narrative: A wide tidal-flat beach on Chungcheongnam-do's west coast, part of Taeanhaean National Park, exposing broad flats at low tide favored for shellfish gathering and coastal walks. Its gentle, shifting shoreline contrasts with the rockier coasts found elsewhere in Korea.

instrumentation: press-line stamping thud, paint-booth mist hiss, engine-line torque wrench
character_short: a 300,000-car-a-year assembly plant building Sonatas and electric IONIQs
narrative: A Hyundai Motor manufacturing plant operating since 1996 with a capacity of roughly 300,000 vehicles a year, now producing electric IONIQ models. It sits a short distance from centuries-old heritage sites, making Asan one of the clearest old-meets-new pairings in this dataset.

instrumentation: thatched-roof wind rustle, stream trickle, wooden gate creak
character_short: a 500-year-old village of thatched and tiled hanok where residents still farm the land
narrative: A roughly 500-year-old preserved yangban (noble-class) village in Asan, still arranged around its original stone walls and traditional houses. Unlike a reconstructed museum village, its layout reflects genuine continuous habitation by descendant families.

instrumentation: pansori vocals, gayageum, slow warmth
character_short: the hometown of bibimbap, hundreds of hanok guesthouses in one dense quarter
narrative: A dense quarter of over 800 traditional hanok houses in continuous use for roughly six centuries, and the UNESCO-recognized birthplace of bibimbap, distinguished locally by bean sprouts, sesame oil, and raw egg yolk. Daily hanji papermaking, fan-making, and calligraphy workshops keep the heritage active rather than static.

instrumentation: solo daegeum, falling-leaf rustle, mountain stream
character_short: a mountain valley considered Korea's finest for autumn foliage
narrative: A mountain valley widely considered Korea's finest destination for autumn foliage, drawing large crowds each October and November for its maple-lined trails. Outside peak season, the same valley reads as sparse and quiet, following a stream through otherwise still forest.

instrumentation: old bank-vault echo, tram-bell ghost, retro film-reel flutter
character_short: a preserved 1920s colonial port street of Japanese banks and warehouses turned museums
narrative: A preserved district of Japanese colonial-era buildings from Korea's 1900-1945 modern period, including a former Chosun Bank branch built in 1922, now organized as an open-air architecture museum. It documents a harder, more contested layer of Korean history than most heritage sites on this list.

instrumentation: gondola cable hum, powder-snow crunch, alpine wind
character_short: Korea's alpine ski resort, a gondola climbing through Deogyusan's high mountain snow
narrative: A ski and mountain resort in Deogyusan National Park, one of Korea's higher-elevation winter sports destinations, with slopes and cable cars built into the surrounding peaks. It gives Jeollabuk-do a genuine winter-sport identity alongside its agricultural and culinary reputation.
photo_artist: Republic of  Korea from Seoul, Republic of Korea

instrumentation: ambient wetland drone, solo oboe, bird calls
character_short: a vast tidal reed marsh at golden hour, cranes overhead
narrative: A vast tidal reed marsh and wetland ecological park, one of Korea's most significant protected coastal wetlands, drawing migratory cranes each winter. Golden-hour light across the reed beds makes it one of the most visually serene sites in this entire dataset.

instrumentation: koto-like pluck, misty hush, distant rooster
character_short: terraced green tea fields disappearing into morning mist
narrative: Korea's largest tea-growing area, cultivated since 1939, with terraced rows of tea bushes disappearing into morning mist and one of the country's longest-running festivals held each spring. The rhythmic geometry of the terraces gives it a distinctive, almost graphic landscape.

instrumentation: bamboo wind chime, rustling leaves, soft flute
character_short: a dense bamboo forest with wind moving through it like static
narrative: A dense bamboo forest park where wind moving through the tall stands produces a constant rustling, static-like sound throughout the grounds. It is one of the purest single-material landscapes in this dataset, built almost entirely around one plant.
photo_artist: UNC - CFC - USFK from Seoul, Republic of Korea

instrumentation: straw-roof wind, well-bucket creak, farmyard rooster
character_short: a 600-year-old walled town still farmed by about 100 households behind stone ramparts
narrative: A genuinely inhabited walled folk village dating to 1397, still home to roughly 100 households living in traditional straw-roofed hanok, unlike purpose-built museum villages elsewhere. Its stone walls and continuous residency have made it a favored filming location for historical Korean dramas.

instrumentation: cable-car pulley hum, harbor-light shimmer, night-market sizzle
character_short: a coastal city famous for its glittering night sea view and cross-harbor cable car
narrative: A coastal city home to the world's largest single-site petrochemical complex, generating nearly half of Korea's national petrochemical output, alongside a scenic night skyline that hosted the 2012 World Expo. It pairs heavy industry directly against a genuinely popular tourist waterfront.

instrumentation: gayageum, slow strings, temple bells
character_short: a 1,000-year former capital where royal burial mounds rise from the city itself
narrative: The former capital of the Silla Kingdom for nearly a thousand years (57 BCE-935 CE), its UNESCO-listed historic areas include Bulguksa Temple, Seokguram Grotto, and Cheomseongdae, Asia's oldest surviving astronomical observatory. Royal burial mounds rising directly within the modern city make Gyeongju function as a living museum rather than a fenced-off site.

instrumentation: mask-dance drum, courtyard echo, wooden clack
character_short: a horseshoe-river folk village famous for traditional mask-dance drama
narrative: A UNESCO-listed clan village on a horseshoe bend of the Nakdong River, still roughly 70% populated by descendants of a single clan practicing centuries-old Confucian household traditions. It is also known for its traditional mask-dance drama, performed there since the Goryeo period.

instrumentation: blast-furnace roar, molten-steel hiss, rolling-mill clang
character_short: one of Korea's founding steel mills, blast furnaces glowing orange along the Pohang coast
narrative: Korea's first integrated steel mill, built in the late 1960s, which transformed Pohang from a fishing port into the country's self-described "Steel Capital." The scale of blast furnaces and rolling mills along the coast makes it one of the most industrially dominant sites in this dataset.

instrumentation: gayageum, valley wind, 500-year-old wooden-beam creak
character_short: Korea's largest traditional clan village, tile-roofed noble houses over 500 years old
narrative: Korea's largest traditional clan village, UNESCO-listed alongside Gyeongju's historic areas, with tile-roofed noble houses over 500 years old set into a wooded valley. Its scale and preservation make it a direct counterpart to Hahoe, from a different clan and a different corner of the same province.
photo_artist: Kok Leng Yeo from Singapore, Singapore

instrumentation: cable-car wind, harbor engine hum, mellow brass
character_short: a hillside harbor city looking out over hundreds of small islands
narrative: A hillside harbor city looking out over hundreds of small islands, reachable partly by a scenic cable car that gives sweeping views across the archipelago. Its layered hillside streets and harbor life give it a naturally cinematic, coastal-town character.
photo_artist: Jungho Jung and User:Asfreeas Derivative work by User:Caspian blue

instrumentation: festival drum, river flow, lantern-float ambience
character_short: a riverside fortress city famous for its autumn floating-lantern festival
narrative: A riverside fortress city on the Namgang River, home to the Namgang Lantern Festival, a tradition dating to 1592 when lanterns were floated to block Japanese river crossings during the Imjin War's siege of Jinjuseong. The fortress walls and river together anchor one of Korea's most historically rooted festival cities.

instrumentation: 900-ton Goliath-crane groan, dry-dock flood roar, steel-hull weld spark
character_short: a shipyard with the world's largest dry dock, building tankers the length of four football fields
narrative: A major shipbuilding complex on Geoje Island including the world's largest single dry dock, central to the local economy alongside a neighboring Samsung Heavy Industries yard. Constant large-scale fabrication and crane activity define this stretch of coastline.

instrumentation: boat-tour engine, sea-cliff echo, gull chorus
character_short: a jagged sea-cliff islet off Geoje reached only by boat, called Korea's Geumgangsan of the sea
narrative: A small, scenic islet off Geoje known for dramatic sea cliffs, sea caves, and a boat-accessible viewing platform, often called one of Korea's most beautiful coastal spots. It offers a sharply different, much quieter counterpoint to the shipyard just up the coast.
photo_artist: Korea.net / Korean Culture and Information Service (Jeon Han)

instrumentation: solo flute, wind, volcanic ambience
character_short: a dormant volcano with a crater lake at its summit, above the clouds
narrative: A dormant shield volcano and South Korea's highest peak, with a crater lake at its summit reachable by trail above the cloud line. It anchors Jeju's UNESCO Natural World Heritage status alongside the island's extensive lava tube systems.

instrumentation: gentle strings, ocean breeze, dawn chorus
character_short: a tuff-cone crater rising from the sea, famous for sunrise
narrative: A tuff-cone crater rising directly from the sea on Jeju's eastern coast, formed by a hydrovolcanic eruption roughly 5,000 years ago and famous as a sunrise viewpoint. It is one of the most recognizable single landforms in the entire Moodscape dataset.

instrumentation: light jazz, tropical guitar, ocean rhythm
character_short: the relaxed island capital, tangerine orchards and black lava-stone walls
narrative: Jeju Island's relaxed capital, mixing tangerine orchards and black volcanic-stone walls with a genuine working port and city center. It functions as the island's practical hub rather than its scenic centerpiece, which lies mostly outside the city.

instrumentation: black-stone wall wind, thatched-roof rustle, horse-hoof clop
character_short: a 600-year-old walled village of black volcanic-stone houses, still lived in today
narrative: A traditional walled village preserving Jeju's distinct vernacular architecture, including black lava-stone walls and low thatched roofs built to withstand the island's strong winds. Its building style is visibly different from mainland Korean folk villages, reflecting Jeju's separate cultural and linguistic history.

instrumentation: cave-drip echo, deep stone resonance, underground silence
character_short: an 8.9km lava tube cave, one of Earth's longest, formed a hundred thousand years ago
narrative: One of the finest lava tube cave systems in the world, part of Jeju's UNESCO Natural World Heritage listing, formed by volcanic activity roughly 200,000 years ago. Its scale — including one of the largest lava columns known in any lava tube — makes it a geological centerpiece of the island.
